title: Euler characteristics of twists by several invertible modules form a numerical polynomial
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and let $\mathcal L_1,\ldots,\mathcal L_r$ be invertible $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-sc-invertible-module]. Then the map $(n_1,\ldots,n_r)\mapsto\chi(X,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L_1^{\otimes n_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal L_r^{\otimes n_r})$ [def-pc-euler-characteristic] from $\mathbf Z^r$ to $\mathbf Z$ is a numerical polynomial in $n_1,\ldots,n_r$ of total degree at most $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

proof.text: For empty support, the stalk criterion [pqf-lem-sheaf-zero-stalks] makes F zero. Tensoring by every invertible signed power preserves zero, and the Euler characteristic vanishes. Choose the zero polynomial, retaining the original separate zero disjunct.

First prove the bounded assertion: if dim Supp(F)≤d for natural d, the Euler function is a polynomial of total degree≤d. Induct on d. In the zero case, apply [lem-pc-chi-zero-dim-support] successively to the list of signed powers. Coherence, support and Euler characteristic are preserved at each fold step, so the constant polynomial works.

In the successor case, use [lem-sc-euler-twist-coordinate-difference] for each j. Apply the induction hypothesis to its coherent modules G_a, all supported in dimension≤d. The polynomial sum of c_a P_a has degree≤d and evaluates to the coordinate difference, including negative exponents.
Apply [lem-sc-coordinate-differences-polynomial] with degree parameter d+1 to integrate these coordinate differences. It gives the desired polynomial of degree≤d+1 on the whole integer lattice.

Properness bounds dim X by a natural number; the dimension of the support subspace is at most dim X. Its dimension is therefore bottom or a natural number. The bottom case was handled above; in the natural case take the exact support dimension as d in the bounded assertion. This proves the unchanged bound in WithBot ENat, using the existing proved HilbertPolynomial helper topologicalKrullDim_le_unbotD_toNat.

lean.statement: theorem exists_mvPolynomial_eulerChar_tensorPowers (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [IsProper (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] (F : X.Modules) (hF : RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace F) (r : ℕ) (L : Fin r → X.Modules) [∀ i : Fin r, (L i).IsInvertible] : ∃ P : MvPolynomial (Fin r) ℚ, (P = 0 ∨ ((P.totalDegree : ℕ∞) : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ topologicalKrullDim {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk F.val.presheaf x)}) ∧ ∀ n : Fin r → ℤ, MvPolynomial.eval (fun i => (n i : ℚ)) P = (((List.ofFn fun i : Fin r => if 0 ≤ n i then (L i).tensorPow (n i).toNat else (L i).dual.tensorPow (-n i).toNat).foldl (fun M N : X.Modules => M ⊗ N) F).eulerChar k : ℚ)
